subject: Dedicated reservation architecture and phaseboarding proposal for LyricAI
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@lyricai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation architecture and phaseboarding proposal for LyricAI

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — really enjoyed the discussion about LyricAI's conversational routing and batch retraining workloads. Attached is a compact proposal and a capacity workbook with three distinct reservation architectures we think will fit your procurement window and performance targets. High-level options: 

- Option A (Anchor-Heavy): 48 anchor GPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent), full-vCPU isolation; predictable throughput, minimal runtime autoscaling. Good if you want tight latency SLAs and long-lived KV caches.
- Option B (Light Anchor + Elastic Burst): 12 anchor GPUs + access to a shared burst pool up to 60 GPUs during peak windows; lower committed baseline, faster time to sign.
- Option C (Micro-Anchor + Credit-based Ramp): 8 anchor GPUs + 30k burst-credit tokens over first 90 days, staged ramp by feature flag. Optimized for teams who want the lowest commit while preserving peak capability.

Key considerations in the workbook: expected 99th-percentile latency for chat (≤120ms/token on anchor), prefix/KV cache hit-rate assumptions, warm-start credit allocation during month 0–3, and an activation wave schedule (week-by-week for the first 12 weeks). We also included a sample procurement timeline and an internal onboarding checklist.

Ask: please review the workbook and let us know which option aligns best with your procurement and security timeline. If you prefer, we can run a brief sizing call Thursday to walk through the cost/tradeoffs and lock down a phased rollout.

Attachments: lyricai_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_proposal_phaseboarding_draft.pdf (proposal).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the clear options and the workbook. A few quick questions from procurement and infra: 

1) Baseline ask: is Option B's 12 anchor GPUs a hard minimum we must commit to, or is there room for an initial 8-GPU anchor that moves to 12 within the first 30 days?
2) Ramp cadence: our procurement team prefers a predictable monthly spend profile. Can you provide a simple month-by-month spend table for Option C's credit model?
3) Autoscale & burst: how fast is the burst pool able to attach GPUs (seconds/minutes)? We need to know for peak SLA planning.

Security note: we need SOC 2 evidence and the onboarding checklist you mentioned to include expected logs and audit retention for 12 months.

If it's helpful, can Ben join a call tomorrow morning PST to go into technical details?

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@lyricai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation architecture and phaseboarding proposal for LyricAI

Samantha — quick technical answers below, pulled from the workbook and infra runbooks. Happy to expand on any item on a call.

Short answers:
- Minimum commitment flexibility: Option B can start at 8 anchor GPUs with a contractual step-up to 12 GPUs within 30 days. We call this a "30-day anchor step"; pricing uses a stepwise pro-rate in month 1.
- Burst attach time: typical attach ~45–90 seconds (depends on region and serialization of intermediate images); we guarantee sub-3min for production peaks in the SLA with warm-warmed images.
- Credit model (Option C): we converted credits to GPU-hours in sheet tab "Credits->Hours"; 30k credits ≈ 2,500 GPU-hours which maps to ~60 peak hours/week for first 4 weeks. See workbook worksheet "MonthByMonth_Credits" for the spend table.

Architectural sketches (tradeoffs):
A) Anchor-Heavy (48 GPUs): 
  - Pros: consistent latency, large KV-cache residency, simplest scheduling.
  - Cons: highest committed cost; slower iteration if workload mix shifts.

B) Light Anchor + Elastic Burst (12 anchor -> 60 peak): 
  - Pros: lower committed baseline, fast burst for daytime traffic spikes, simpler procurement signature.
  - Cons: slightly higher per-peak unit cost vs. anchors, requires warm image maintenance to meet 99p.
  - Suggestion: enable prefix caching for chat pipelines and reserve 25% of burst pool capacity for LyricAI during agreed peak windows.

C) Micro-Anchor + Credits (8 anchor + credits): 
  - Pros: lowest upfront commit; very cost-effective for unpredictable startups.
  - Cons: more operational touchpoints early (credit consumption monitoring), potential cold-starts without warmup credits.

Operational controls we recommend across all options:
- Weekly ramp checkpoints for first 12 weeks (cost & perf review).
- Canary feature routing for new model variants (10% traffic toggles).
- Warmup/idle retention policy: keep 2–3 images warmed during business hours for rapid attach.

Docs attached to this message: short SLO table, MonthByMonth_Credits export, onboarding checklist (PDF stub).

Next steps: confirm whether you want the 30-day anchor step in the contract and which option to frame in procurement. Once we have that, Marissa will prepare the implementation milestones and initial runbook for the onboarding call.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@lyricai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation architecture and phaseboarding proposal for LyricAI

Samantha — following Ben's notes, here's a pragmatic path we recommend to align procurement speed and risk: 

Recommendation (single path): Option B with the 30-day anchor step (start at 8 GPUs, step to 12 within 30 days), and a staged ramp to 60 GPUs over three months in three waves:

- Wave 0 (Week 0–2): 8 anchor GPUs on production; enable prefix caching and warm two model images.
- Wave 1 (Week 3–6): step to 12 anchor GPUs; enable burst pool reservation of up to 25% during agreed windows.
- Wave 2 (Week 7–12): enable autoscale up to 60 GPUs, add two additional warm images and start A/B rollout of model v2.

Procurement notes:
- We'll include a contractual 30-day step clause in the SOW and prorate month 1 charges.
- Warm-start credits: provide 10k credits upfront to smooth the first 30 days (tracked in the workbook).
- SOC 2: we'll bundle evidence and the onboarding checklist in the admin portal link and provide audit logs for 12 months by default.

Implementation kickoff: please sign the attached draft SOW and we will schedule a 30-min implementation plan meeting (proposed times: Tue 4/17 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 4/18 08:00–08:30 PT). DocuSign link included in the related links.

If LyricAI confirms Option B + 30-day step, we will: 
1) Lock the SOW and issue an initial invoice for the pro-rated anchor.
2) Provision the anchor lane in the target region (us-west-2) and seed warm images.
3) Share the onboarding runbook and invite your infra leads to the kickoff.

Looking forward — happy to jump on the call with Ben to walk the workbook line-by-line.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
